name: Terah
title: Abraham's father
summary: Terah was the son of Nahor and the father of Abram (Abraham), Nahor, and Haran. He is known for leading his family out of Ur of the Chaldeans with the aim of traveling to the land of Canaan, but settled in Haran where he died. Terah represents the transition between the early generations after the flood and the time of the patriarchs.

keyEvents.title: Terah's birth and lineage
keyEvents.description: Terah was born as the son of Nahor, in the line of Shem, Noah's son. He is part of the important genealogy that leads from Shem to Abram.

keyEvents.title: Father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran
keyEvents.description: Terah became the father of three sons: Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Through Abram, God would establish his covenant with a chosen people.

keyEvents.title: Haran's death in Ur
keyEvents.description: Haran, the son of Terah, died in Ur of the Chaldeans, his native land, while his father Terah was still living. Haran left behind his son Lot.

keyEvents.title: Departure from Ur of the Chaldeans
keyEvents.description: Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (the son of Haran), and his daughter-in-law Sarai, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. This marked the beginning of a historic journey that would shape God's plan of salvation.

keyEvents.title: Settlement in Haran
keyEvents.description: Instead of continuing on to Canaan, Terah and his family settled in Haran. They remained there, and Terah never completed the journey to the promised land.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Terah in Haran
keyEvents.description: Terah died in Haran at the age of 205. After his death, God called Abram to leave Haran and go on to the land of Canaan. Joshua later notes that Terah served other gods.
